issue.title: Provider.useFactory called multiple times
issue.body:
**I'm submitting a ...**  (check one with "x")
```
[X] bug report => search github for a similar issue or PR before submitting
[ ] feature request
[ ] support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
```

**Current behavior**
When upgrading from Angular 2.1.2 to the current 2.2.3, the semantics of an NgModule provider changed, when it was using the useFactory property. In 2.1.2, the factory method was only called once and effectively gave a singleton to each injection point within the NgModule. Now, it is being called multiple times for each injection point.
Is this expected?

**Expected behavior**
The Provider.useFactory is only called one time per NgModule and all injection points in components it is injected into.

**Please tell us about your environment:**
OS: Windows 7 x64
IDE: IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate 2016.3
Package Manager: npm 4.0.2
TypeScript: 2.0.10

* **Angular version:** 2.2.3

* **Browser:** Chrome 54.0.2840.99 m (64-bit)
 
* **Language:** TypeScript 2.0.10 ES2015

body:
Same problem here. Everything worked flawlessly with Angular 2.1.2 and Router 3.1.2. After upgrading to Angular 2.2.3 and Router 3.2.3 -> boom! When I added a constructor() to the module, I could confirm that even the whole module was instantiated multiple times, and not just the provider declared within that module. The module was activated lazily with a:
```
{
    path: 'somepath',
    loadChildren: 'app/somepath/somepath.module#SomePathModule'
}
```
inside an app.routing.ts, which is included in an `RouterModule.forRoot(appRoutes)` which itself is added to the `imports` statement of the app.module.ts's NgModule.

issue.body:
This took be far more effort than I expected ... and it's still not working perfectly.
This commit will add AoT-compilation as an alternative to the regular dist build. It's not the default since AoT (and thus the @ngtools/webpack plugin as well) is not only still a little bit ... incomplete, but also
requires a particular code-style and structure that has to be fulfilled by your own code as well as by the code of the libraries you're using. This might not hold true in your particular case, thus I'd suggest it's better to have both options available.

What still need to be done:
- [x] ~~Figure out why the shared module is instantiated multiple times - it's possible to work around the result (multiple setup of the translate service), but I'd be better to kick off the original cause. Seems to be related to https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/12889 - iirc this has not been an issue in 2.1.x~~. Moved the translation service init part to the application module; the shared module appears to be the wrong place for this.

issue.title: Lazy loading module and injected service behaviour
issue.body:
**I'm submitting a ...** (check one with "x") ``` [x] bug report => search github for a similar issue or PR before submitting [ ] feature request [ ] support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question ``` **Current behavior** Service instance is created whenever lazy module is loaded. It is not created only once when module loaded and not preserved in DI context. Even further service instance not preserved for component too. Each time lazy module loaded for any of component path the service instance would be created. Service instance not being shared between components of the lazy module. Even service instance not being preserved for a single component for reuse. **Expected behavior** Service instance is created whenever eager module initially loaded, and the instance would be shared among all components of the module. I expect same behaviour with lazy module too. Service should be created once lazy module loaded and should remain in DI context of the module and should be available for all components in the module. **Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions** My code is here: https://github.com/mananvpanchal/angular2-webpack-boilerplate please clone it and just run `npm install` and then `npm run start`. If you want to code your own: Just create a lazy module and create two component in the module. Create a service which should be provided by the module. You can see that the service instance will be created each time you try to load the lazy module including any of two component. I am putting here little code snippet as well. ``` const routerConfig = [ { path: "", component: LazyComponent }, { path: "otherlazy", component: OtherLazyComponent } ]; @NgModule({ imports: [ RouterModule.forChild(routerConfig) ], declarations: [ LazyComponent, OtherLazyComponent ], exports: [ LazyComponent, OtherLazyComponent ], providers: [ PrivateService ] }) export class LazyModule { } ``` ``` @Component({ selector: 'lazy', template: `

Lazy

{{ps.getId()}}
` }) export class LazyComponent { constructor(private ps : PrivateService) { } incr() { this.ps.incr(); } } ``` ``` @Component({ selector: 'other-lazy', template: `

Other Lazy

{{ps.getId()}}
` }) export class OtherLazyComponent { constructor(private ps : PrivateService) { } incr() { this.ps.incr(); } } ``` ``` @Injectable() export class PrivateService { id = 0; incr() { this.id++; } getId() { return this.id; } } ``` ```LazyOther Lazy``` If I click `Lazy` and I hit `` I can see the value `{{ps.getId()}}` would increment. But, if I go to `Other Lazy` I get `0`. If I again increment here and I go back to `Lazy` I again get `0`. **What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior?** **Please tell us about your environment:** * **Angular version:** 2.0.X * **Browser:** [all | Chrome XX | Firefox XX | IE XX | Safari XX | Mobile Chrome XX | Android X.X Web Browser | iOS XX Safari | iOS XX UIWebView | iOS XX WKWebView ] * **Language:** [all | TypeScript X.X | ES6/7 | ES5] * **Node (for AoT issues):** `node --version` = v5.4.0
